original_question: Describe the differential geometry of shape spaces carrying the nonlocal H^{-1/2} metrics that arise from dynamic free boundaries or vortex sheets in hydrodynamics.
target_in_paper: Problem 36 in §13 (Singular Vorticities in the Euler Equation): Describe the differential geometry of shape spaces equipped with such H^{-1/2}-metrics obtained as metrics on dynamic boundaries or vortex sheets.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open-problem type (to describe the differential geometry), the correct geometric object (shape spaces), the specific Sobolev order/nonlocality (H^{-1/2}), and the hydrodynamic origin in vortex sheets and dynamic/free boundaries. It is very close to the paper’s official formulation.
missing_details: The paper does not mean arbitrary shape spaces: the metric is described on the space of closed hypersurfaces bounding the same fixed volume in a fixed ambient fluid domain/manifold.
The nearby context gives an explicit equivalent viewpoint: instead of hypersurfaces, one may work with constant densities supported inside those hypersurfaces.
The H^{-1/2} metric is not just any fractional Sobolev metric; it is the specific nonlocal metric constructed with the help of Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators.
The paper records an important structural fact about this metric: it is nondegenerate because it is bounded below by the Kantorovich-Wasserstein distance.
The hydrodynamic meaning of the metric should be stated: its geodesics describe motions of potential fluid flows with vortex sheets and fluids with free dynamic boundary.

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, the ambient domain/manifold and the regularity class of the hypersurfaces should be fixed explicitly; Problem 36 itself leaves these analytic details implicit.

The phrase 'describe the differential geometry' is intended in the Arnold-style sense used earlier in the paper, i.e. questions about geodesic geometry, curvature, conjugate points, and related structures, even though Problem 36 itself does not enumerate these subquestions.
No algebraic data such as ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; this is a differential-geometric hydrodynamics problem.
refined_question: For a fixed ambient fluid domain or Riemannian manifold, describe the differential geometry of the shape space of closed hypersurfaces enclosing a prescribed volume, equipped with the hydrodynamically induced nonlocal H^{-1/2} metric defined via Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators, whose geodesics describe potential fluid motions with vortex sheets or with free dynamic boundary.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, describe the differential geometry of the space of constant densities supported inside equal-volume closed hypersurfaces, equipped with the same hydrodynamically induced H^{-1/2} metric.
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 36, not the earlier groupoid-curvature Problem 3, because §13 is the only place where the paper explicitly introduces a nonlocal H^{-1/2} metric on shape spaces and immediately formulates the corresponding open problem. The paragraph before Problem 36 supplies the missing scope: the shapes are closed hypersurfaces bounding the same volume; equivalently, one can view them as constant densities inside those hypersurfaces; the metric is built from Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators; it is nondegenerate; and its geodesics model potential flows with vortex sheets or free dynamic boundary. Problem 3 in §2.2 is still relevant only as the paper’s clearest nearby explanation of what the authors mean by 'describe the differential geometry' in Arnold’s sense.
